thread:
Mia Chen: Hey team — Driftwood POC just surfaced a blocker: their custom tokenizer produces different token counts vs our catalog model. They want to run Llama-Adapter-13B variant; embeddings/semantics look fine but generation truncates. Any quick checks?
Samir Patel: Oof. Is this the q4 tokenizer or a modified byte-fallback?
Mia Chen: Modified. They said they switched unk-handling and it's shifting offsets. Example: 'The quick' -> tokenized to 5 tokens for them, 4 for our Llama-Adapter.
Jordan Lee: Can you paste a minimal repro?
Mia Chen: Sure — snippet from their app:```python
text = "The quick brown fox jumps"
# their tokenizer -> [101, 202, ...] len=7
# our model tokenizer -> len=6
```
Samir Patel: Likely mismatch in tokenizer config (add_prefix_space / bos handling). If offsets shift, KV cache alignment breaks and you get truncated sequences or garbled continuation.
Oliver (infra): Also check vocab size & special token ids. If they remapped <pad>/<eos> we may be hitting early stopping.
Mia Chen: They mentioned they ran quantization for latency too (4-bit). Could that change behavior?
Jordan Lee: Quantization shouldn't change tokenizer behavior but if they used a custom conversion that altered the model's embedding matrix indexing, yeah. Ask for their converter log.
Mia Chen: Copying what they sent: "converter: llm-convert v2 -> success, warnings: token_map_mismatch detected for ids 5023..5030"
Samir Patel: Token map mismatch = red flag. We need mapping or align token ids back to the model's vocab. Short-term: recommend they switch to our tokenizer bundle (we host it in catalog) and retokenize inputs for POC.
Mia Chen: They'll push to try that. What about pricing/SLA asks? They asked if we can guarantee p99 latency <120ms for 8k context on dedicated capacity and custom model variant.
Oliver (infra): For a dedicated pool with 2xA100 or equivalent GPU we can target p99 ~80-140ms depending on batching. Recommend reserved capacity + burst. I can draft a sizing note.
Samir Patel: Also flag support for secure keyring — they require KMS + HSM attestation in questionnaire. Do we have an integration for their vendor?
Jordan Lee: We support KMS and can integrate with customer HSM for Private deployments; for Hosted we can offer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) via Redwood Private on VPC.
Mia Chen: Got it. They also want evidence for SOC2 + encryption in transit at rest.
Samir Patel: Send the compliance packet link: https://redwood.ai/compliance/soc2 and point to the private deployment option.
Mia Chen: I'll send that. Any ops-runbook for quick triage if tokenizer mismatch persists?
Oliver (infra): Yes — short checklist: 1) confirm tokenizer bundle & version; 2) check special token ids; 3) retokenize sample and compare lengths; 4) run small reproduce on our hosted sandbox using their input but our tokenizer; 5) if mismatch persists, request their converter artifact and token_map. I can add commands.
Jordan Lee: Sample command to compare tokenizers:```bash
# using python tokenizers
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer.from_file('their.json').encode('The quick').tokens)"
python -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; print(AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('redwood/llama-adapter-13b').tokenize('The quick'))"
```
Mia Chen: Perfect. I'll run the checklist with them and circle back. Any objections if I offer a 2-week Dedicated trial at estimated cost + 2-week engineering support for adapter mapping?
Samir Patel: Sounds reasonable. Pricing note: include conversion support as a scoped SOW; don't promise code changes to their converter.
Oliver (infra): I'll draft sizing + SLA language. Jordan — can you add a short note about tokenizer mapping risks for legal/security?
Jordan Lee: On it, will include risk language and mitigation steps.
Mia Chen: Great — looping in the Driftwood contact now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
